summary: The narrator, half-conscious and disoriented, leaves a room and steps into a dark hallway, intending to say a last farewell to Tz'ac Tzotz, one of Sarah's children. Marcelina, in a white shift, appears and tells her that everyone is praying for her and that it is almost time, but she won't reveal where Sarah is. The narrator finds the children's room empty, realizes she should have gone straight to the lab, and then the power dies and heavy boots pound up the stairs.
one_line: A disoriented narrator searches the dark hallways for Tz'ac Tzotz and Sarah, and finds the children already gone as hostile footsteps approach.
key_facts: The narrator quietly pulled back the door and peered into a dark hallway that was empty, with no snakes and only a light breeze.
The narrator's main wish upon stepping out was to see Tz'ac Tzotz one last time, described as a last farewell to one of Sarah's children.
Marcelina, wearing a white shift, told the narrator that they were all praying for her and that it was almost time.
Marcelina reached out to help the narrator stand when the narrator was tripping with reality almost gone.
The narrator asked Marcelina where Sarah was, and Marcelina said Sarah had been looking forward to the ceremony and wanted them to bring her.
Marcelina said 'They all love her' and 'They're taking good care of her' when asked about Sarah.
The narrator asked Marcelina to promise to stop all this, calling it horrible and sad, and Marcelina replied, 'It's our life.'
The narrator was terrified Alex Goddard might materialize and pulled away to climb the stairs.
The narrator went to her room at the end of the hall and slipped her passport and a charge card into her pants pocket.
The room of Tz'ac Tzotz and his mother was empty, with the crib also empty, indicating the children had already been taken.
The narrator realized she had been a fool not to head straight for the lab.
The main power abruptly died or was deliberately shut off, plunging the room and hallway into pitch-black darkness.
A thunder of hard boots was heard pounding up the steps.
